meta.title: Health & Safety: looking after yourself, looking after each other

questions.prompt: Which of these 'switch noticing back on'? Select all that apply.
options: Take two seconds — is this normal, or has it just become normal?
Say it out loud to one other person
Treat a near miss as information, not an embarrassment
Move on quickly so nobody notices
questions.explanation: The three things that switch noticing back on are the two-second check, saying it out loud, and treating near misses as information.

questions.prompt: Why must you not assume the fire evacuation route is the same as another room you use?
options: All routes are the same — the signs are uniform
Studios, computer labs and production spaces have different exits
There is only one exit per building
Routes only matter at lunch time
questions.explanation: Different rooms and buildings have different exits — confirm the route for the specific room you're in.

questions.prompt: The deck says messing with someone's camera rig 'as a joke' is…
options: A safety issue with someone else's name on it
Only a problem if the camera is expensive
questions.explanation: 'Messing with someone's camera rig "as a joke" isn't banter — it's a safety issue with someone else's name on it.'

questions.prompt: Which programme uses COSHH substances and requires gloves and eye protection?
options: Darkroom / analogue photography — developer, stop bath, fixer
questions.explanation: Darkroom/analogue photography uses developer, stop bath and fixer — these are COSHH chemicals; gloves and eye protection are mandatory.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for any location filming, a written ____ assessment must be approved by your tutor before any off-campus shoot.
questions.template: For any location filming, a written ____ assessment must be approved by your tutor before any off-campus shoot.
questions.explanation: A written risk assessment approved by your tutor is required before any off-campus shoot.

questions.prompt: The deck widens reporting beyond physical hazards. Which of these counts too?
options: A space, an activity, or someone's behaviour that has made you feel uncomfortable or unsafe
Only things that happen in studios
questions.explanation: Reporting covers hazards and anything — a space, an activity, the way someone's behaving — that's made you feel uncomfortable or unsafe.
